basis: Inherited corneal endothelial dystrophy; disease is confined to the eye.
Hindbrain malformation with cranial nerve dysfunction; permanent sensorineural hearing loss affects most patients. Cardiac and skeletal anomalies are variable.
Glutathione metabolism defect causes erythrocyte hemolysis; cataracts reported in 3/3 patients. Hyperbilirubinemia reflects hemolysis, not hepatic damage.
Manganese transport disorder causes degenerative dystonia; fixed joint contractures occur in 3/9 and scoliosis in 30-79%. Hepatic disease is not characteristic of this subtype.
Umbrella of congenital skeletal muscle diseases. Respiratory weakness reflects muscle dysfunction; intrinsic lung or cardiac disease is not common across the group.
Defining cerebellar/brainstem malformation and developmental impairment; retinal dysplasia and renal cysts are occasional. Hepatic fibrosis 2/7 is borderline and omitted.
Syndromic skeletal growth restriction with characteristic fifth-finger clinodactyly. Neurologic, cardiac and hypoglycemic manifestations are annotated as occasional.
Inherited impairment of platelet responsiveness is a blood-cell functional disorder.
Corneal stromal dystrophy causes opacification, erosions and visual impairment; no systemic metabolic organ disorder is established by the supplied evidence.
Renal magnesium wasting defines the electrolyte disorder; intellectual disability, developmental delay and seizures were reported in 2/2 patients.
Mycobacterial infection predominantly involving the lungs; individual extrapulmonary organ sites do not meet the common-involvement threshold across the umbrella.
Renal tubular salt-handling disorder defined by hyperkalemia, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis and hypertension.
Sellar CNS tumor with frequent pituitary dysfunction; optic pathway compression causes progressive visual loss or field defects in 30-79%, independent of treatment.
Microphthalmia defines this umbrella; associated extraocular organ abnormalities vary by syndrome and cannot be generalized across the group.
Schwann-cell tumor arising from peripheral nerves in the posterior mediastinum; mediastinal location alone does not establish pulmonary involvement.
Congenital deficiency of radial forearm and hand skeletal structures.
Hormone-secreting adenoma arising in the adrenal cortex.
Neoplasms arise in the vagina, a reproductive organ outside the defined axes.
Telomere biology disorder defined by pulmonary fibrosis and/or hypocellular bone marrow failure.
Disorders of central cognitive processing and perception, including neglect and agnosia; sensory-organ damage is not required.
Developmental small-eye disorder with severe hyperopia and abnormal ocular anatomy; associated glaucoma remains within the ocular axis.
Male breast tissue enlargement; breast has no axis, and an underlying endocrine gland disorder is not intrinsic to this concept.
Neurologic movement disorder affecting multiple noncontiguous body regions; dystonic contractions alone do not establish skeletal muscle damage.
Hypertrichosis and neuropathy define syndrome; periostitis occurs in 30-79%; retinal anomalies described in 3/4 cases. Secondary osteomyelitis is a separate infection.
Congenital tricuspid valve and papillary muscle malformation; possible hepatomegaly from congestion does not establish common hepatic damage.
